articles.title: Police warn residents of late-night armed robberies in Bronzeville, Lake Meadows
articles.description:
Chicago police are alerting the public about multiple armed robberies that occurred in Bronzeville and Lake Meadows this month.

In each of the area's robberies, police said one to three assailants are believed to have approached victims at night, armed with guns and demanding their mobile phones.

Police in a news bulletin indicated the suspects ordered victims to unlock their phones before taking the devices and fleeing the scene on foot.

The areas where the reported robberies happened include:

  • 400 block of East 32nd Street on Aug. 6 at 10:15 p.m.
  • 400 block of East 32nd Street on Aug. 14 at 11:45 p.m.
  • 3000 block of South State Street on Aug. 14 at 11:45 p.m.

Police described the suspects as three men and one woman, all wearing hooded sweatshirts.

Area residents are urged to remain aware of their surroundings and report any suspicious activity immediately, police said.

Anyone with information is encouraged to contact Area 1 detectives at 312-747-8380 or submit an anonymous tip at CPDTIP.com and provide reference number P26-1-070.

articles.title: I’d heard ringing in my ears before. This time, it didn’t stop
articles.description: Miranda Luby was only 36 years old when her tinnitus arrived in the middle of the night, without warning and for no clear reason One night two years ago I was lying in bed when I began to hear a high-pitched, electronic hum. The scene that followed would be comical if it wasn’t so traumatic. I roamed around the house in my PJs, frantically pressing my ears against various electrical appliances. It took half an hour to realise the sound was coming from inside my own head. I’d heard ringing in my ears before, rising then falling, like a one-note crescendo of an orchestra. As a kid I used to believe the myth it was the sound of dying ear cells, playing a swan song for a frequency I’d never hear again. This was different. This time, it didn’t stop. Continue reading...
